BERT and GPT are both transformer-based language models, but they have fundamental differences in their architecture and training approaches:

## **Architecture & Training Direction**

**BERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers)**
- Uses **bidirectional** training - looks at text from both left-to-right and right-to-left simultaneously
- Based on the transformer **encoder** architecture
- Uses masked language modeling (MLM) - randomly masks 15% of tokens and predicts them using surrounding context

**GPT (Generative Pre-trained Transformer)**
- Uses **unidirectional** (left-to-right) training
- Based on the transformer **decoder** architecture  
- Uses autoregressive language modeling - predicts the next token based only on previous tokens

## **Primary Use Cases**

**BERT**
- Excels at understanding and classification tasks
- Text classification, sentiment analysis
- Question answering
- Named entity recognition
- Sentence similarity

**GPT**
- Excels at generation tasks
- Text generation and completion
- Creative writing
- Conversational AI
- Code generation

## **Key Differences Summary**

| Aspect | BERT | GPT |
|--------|------|-----|
| Training | Bidirectional | Unidirectional |
| Architecture | Encoder-only | Decoder-only |
| Objective | Masked token prediction | Next token prediction |
| Best for | Understanding/Analysis | Generation |
| Context | Full sentence context | Only previous context |

Both models revolutionized NLP, but BERT is typically better for tasks requiring deep understanding of text relationships, while GPT excels at generating coherent, contextual text.
